Interface LogProperty

@CaseChanging public interface LogProperty
Describes a key (or several fallback keys) resolved against a LogProperties instance - start with LogProperties.forKey(String) - and also serves as the namespace for the shared property machinery: LogProperty.Result, LogProperty.Validator, and the property-specific exceptions.

    LogProperty.Result<T>

    static interface 
    LogProperty.ValidatedResult<T>
    A LogProperty.Result that is safe to pull a value out of - either because it can never actually be missing (LogProperty.RequiredResult: a LogProperty.Result.Success or an LogProperty.Result.Error, both already resolved one way or the other) or because a caller has explicitly acknowledged the possibility of a still-LogProperty.Result.Missing result by running it through LogProperty.Result.validate(Validator), LogProperty.Result.validateIfError(Validator), or LogProperty.Result.validateNow(Class).
    static final class 
    LogProperty.ValidationException
    Thrown by LogProperty.Validator.validate() when one or more of the accumulated LogProperty.Results failed, reporting every failure in a single message instead of just the first one encountered.
    static class 
    LogProperty.Validator
    Accumulates LogProperty.Results from one or more property lookups and validates them together, so that a caller resolving several properties in sequence can report every failure at once instead of failing fast on the first bad property.

    • ofBoolean

      default LogProperty.Result<Boolean> ofBoolean()
      Resolves the property as a boolean.

      Boolean.parseBoolean(String) treats any value other than "true" (case-insensitive) as false - a typo or a reasonable-looking alternative like someFlag=yes silently resolves to false instead of failing loudly. Component/plugin authors implementing a new property should prefer a small enum (with true/false aliased to e.g. on/off members) parsed via ofString() instead, so a bad value alerts rather than silently resolving false. This method remains available (and fine) for end users setting an existing boolean property.

      Returns:
      result.

    • providingError

      static <U> LogProperty.Result.Error<U> providingError(LogProperty.Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e)
      Like richError(Result.Success, Exception) but for a property whose value was used to invoke LogProvider.provide(String, LogConfig) rather than a plain same-property type conversion - see provideValue(Result, String, LogConfig). The provider constructs a genuinely separate component with its own property tree, so a failure inside it (typically already a complete, self-describing LogProperty.ValidationException of its own) must not be labeled "Error converting property": this property's own value converted just fine, it merely triggered a provider that failed on its own terms.
      Type Parameters:
      U - the provided component type.
      Parameters:
      previousResult - the success whose value was provided from.
      e - the provisioning failure.
      Returns:
      a rich error result.

    • provideValue

      static <T> LogProperty.Result<T> provideValue(LogProperty.Result<LogProvider<T>> providerResult, String name, LogConfig config)
      Like LogProperty.Result.map(PropertyFunction) but specifically for the "resolve to a LogProvider, then provide" step used by output/encoder/appender resolution. A plain LogProperty.Result.map(LogProperty.PropertyFunction) would relabel any failure from provide(...) as "Error converting property" even though this property's own value converted to a provider just fine - see providingError(Result.Success, Exception).
      Type Parameters:
      T - component type.
      Parameters:
      providerResult - an already-resolved provider, e.g. from ofProvider(PropertyFunction).
      name - component name passed to LogProvider.provide(String, LogConfig).
      config - config passed to LogProvider.provide(String, LogConfig).
      Returns:
      the provided component, or the same LogProperty.Result.Missing/ LogProperty.Result.Error a plain conversion would have produced.

    • require

      static <T> T require(String key, @Nullable T value)
      Checks that value is not null, throwing LogProperty.PropertyMissingException naming key if it is. Useful for a property that is required but was set programmatically (e.g. a builder setter) rather than resolved through ofString()/etc, so there is no LogProperty.Result to check for missing-ness.
      Type Parameters:
      T - value type.
      Parameters:
      key - property key, used only in the exception message.
      value - value to check.
      Returns:
      value, never null.
      Throws:
      LogProperty.PropertyMissingException - if value is null.

      default LogProperty or(String fallbackKey)
      Adds a fallback key to try (without {name} interpolation) if none of the keys tried so far are found. Keys already added are tried first, in order; this one is tried last.
